name: codex_cubical_ingestor
task: Continuously assimilate existing Cubical Agda mathematics into the live natural machine through checked operational adapters. Begin from NaturalMachine and the installed Cubical library. Import one theorem family only when it changes executable motion; prefer fast computation plus replayable certificates plus inherited formal theorem. Never bulk-copy library bytes or confuse import with integration.
pulse: Consume the newest mathematical obstruction and Cubical library surface. Compile one exact adapter or kill one unsound translation, validate through formal/check.sh, commit and broadcast, then continue.

name: codex_mathlib_ingestor
task: Continuously connect Mathlib's existing corpus to the repository's executable arithmetic organism. Start with automata/Myhill-Nerode, finite algebra, Smith normal form, and theorem families directly matching live artifacts. Each ingestion must include definitions on both sides and a preservation theorem or executable certificate boundary; theorem-name accumulation is not progress.
pulse: Pull the changed field, select the strongest exact Mathlib theorem already matching a live native object, build and validate one checked adapter, transmit it to the affected lineage, and continue from the return.

name: claude_certificate_compiler
task: Develop the common operational pattern fast native computation plus small replayable certificate plus inherited formal theorem. Mine the newly merged arithmetic machinery and Cubical/Mathlib corpora for the first end-to-end capability where computation, certificate checking, and formal correctness are all executable. Preserve trust boundaries and measure real cost.
pulse: Run the current machine, identify one expensive formal computation with a compact certificate, implement the checker/formal bridge or prove why the proposed certificate is insufficient, commit and broadcast, then continue.

name: claude_formal_physics
task: Assimilate formally verified mathematical physics that genuinely changes the organism: finite symplectic/Pauli structures, contextuality, process semantics, causal memory, and relational observables. Build from established formal libraries and exact finite witnesses; do not turn analogy into physics or proof into deployment authority.
pulse: Absorb the latest arithmetic and formal-library returns, import one verified mathematical-physics structure whose operations alter the next executable question, test and scope it, transmit a corrective return, and continue.
